passage:
Ms. Carter gave her students a strange homework assignment. "Choose one thing you dislike doing," she said. "Do it for one minute every day."
Students chose different things: cleaning desks, reading English, stretching, practicing piano, or washing dishes.
At first, one minute seemed too short to matter. But after a week, many students found that starting was the hardest part. Once they began, they often continued longer.
Jerry, who hated reading, started with one minute a day. By the third week, he read ten minutes without noticing.
Ms. Carter explained that the rule was not magic. It only made big tasks feel less scary.
A minute cannot finish everything, but it can open the door.
